Introduced reforms in public education.

questions.text: Write a short note on Madakari Nayaka.
questions.text_as_printed: Write a short note on Madakari Nayaka. (Average )

answer.value:
Madakari Nayaka was the most powerful and famous ruler among the Chitradurga Nayakas.
He ascended the throne of Chitradurga at the age of 12.
Jealous of his growing power, Hyder Ali of Mysore laid siege to the seven-fortified Chitradurga Fort.
When Hyder Ali's soldiers tried to enter the fort through a secret passage, the brave woman Onake Obavva killed many enemy soldiers using only a wooden pestle (Onake).
In the final fierce battle, Madakari Nayaka was defeated. After capturing him, Hyder Ali brought the rule of the Chitradurga Nayakas to an end.

Onake Obavva is remembered as a symbol of extraordinary bravery, patriotism, and sacrifice, and her name remains immortal in the history of Karnataka.

questions.text_as_printed: Why did Rani Chennamma of Kittur revolt against the British? (Average )

Rani Chennamma was a brave queen of Kittur and the younger wife of Mallasarja Desai.
She adopted Shivalinga Rudra Sarja and began to rule the kingdom.
The British East India Company disputed the adoption, leading to conflict.
Chennamma resisted British rule and their oppressive policies.
Thackeray attacked Kittur with 500 soldiers, but Chennamma fought bravely with 6,000 soldiers.
Despite her bravery, she was betrayed by her own men and imprisoned at Bailhongal.
She is remembered as one of the first Indian women to resist British rule.
Her legacy is still celebrated in folk songs (Lavani).

questions.text_as_printed: Discuss the Hyderabad-Karnataka liberation struggle (Difficult )

answer.value:
Hyderabad-Karnataka Liberation Struggle
The struggle against the Nizam's rule in Hyderabad was a heroic and tumultuous chapter in history. It was marked by great sacrifices and bravery. Hindus in Hyderabad faced dire circumstances under the Nizam's rule. The Nizam's "Kalaghoda" forces were notorious for their brutality. Notable leaders of the struggle included Swami Dayananda, Hardekar Manjappa, and Ramachandra Rao, who started the "Vande Mataram" movement. In 1947, India gained independence, but Hyderabad remained under Nizam rule until September 17, 1948, when Indian forces liberated it, and it merged with India.

Sangolli Rayanna was a brave warrior and a key figure in the Kittur rebellion. He was a loyal companion to Rani Chennamma and a fierce patriot. Rayanna conducted guerrilla warfare against the British, raiding their offices and treasuries. He was a thorn in the side of the British, who saw him as a formidable opponent. Unfortunately, Rayanna was betrayed by traitors and captured by the British. He, along with six companions, was hanged by the British. Rayanna's samadhi (memorial) is located in Nandagad.
